# IDEA Humor Ledger
**Version 1.4 - 2026-08-25**

The anti-repetition record for every humor insertion in an IDEA or Team 5669 artifact. Governed by `IDEA_HUMOR_STANDARDS.md`. Read before the Step 6b humor pass, written in the same pass as delivery.

**This file is the mechanism, not a log.** Cooldowns are enforced by reading it. An insertion that never reached the ledger will be regenerated by a future session that has no way to know it was already used, and repetition is the failure mode humor is least able to survive.

---

## How to use it

**Before the humor pass.** Read the Insertions table. Any candidate matching a live cooldown is rejected at the table and shown struck through with the blocking row named.

**At delivery.** Add one row per insertion, including insertions that were generated and then cut. A cut row is load-bearing: it records that a reference was considered and rejected, which stops the next session from proposing it again and reaching the same conclusion.

**Cooldowns**, all per audience cohort, from the standard:

| Unit | Cooldown | Exempt |
|---|---|---|
| Reference key | 12 months | recurring house-cast characters, which are not references |
| Format id | 3 decks | `A1 Callback` |
| Source universe | 1 per deck, 2 per semester | native formats, which have no universe |
| Within a unit | no format repeats at all | none |

**Per-deck insertion counts are no longer capped**, per `IDEA_HUMOR_STANDARDS.md` 2.1. The cooldowns above are untouched and are still hard: they prevent repetition, which is a different failure from density and the one this file exists for.

**Audience cohorts.** A cooldown is scoped to the room that saw it. Cohorts currently tracked: `FSP-2026` (incoming freshmen, summer program), `IDEA100-F26` (freshman rotation), `IDEA209H-F26` (all three sections, which run identical pacing so they count as one cohort), `FRC-5669` (team members), `FLL` (elementary and middle school teams and their families), `PARENT` (any parent-facing room), `STAFF`.

**Cross-cohort reuse is allowed and encouraged.** A reference retired for `FSP-2026` is fully available for `FRC-5669`. The cooldown protects a room from noticing a habit, and a different room has not seen the habit.

---

## Overheard log

**The only true currency authority.** Per `IDEA_HUMOR_STANDARDS.md` 2.0, web sources surface a reference at the moment it becomes legible to adults, which is the moment it dies with students. What replaces them is what Mr. Pina actually hears quoted in the shop, the hallway, and the pit.

No structure required. Date, what was heard, and where. Chat reads this before proposing any current-band reference and proposes nothing from this band that does not appear here.

| Date | Heard | Where |
|---|---|---|
| | | |

## Calibration record

Six rating rounds, 2026-08-24 to 2026-08-25, which produced the 2.0 gates. Kept because the rejects are as load-bearing as the passes: a format on the permanent-reject list was rejected for a recorded reason, and without that reason a future session regenerates it. Chat did exactly this four times with the crude-drawing family before recognizing it as a gate.

**Passed:** Drake, distracted boyfriend, two buttons, trolley problem, expanding brain (strongest of all six rounds), Spy Kids zoom, Stonks, Gru's plan, 3000 years later (filler tier), Scooby Doo mask, tier list, Uno draw 25, Gigachad, deep fry, rubric ambush, fake comment section, absurdist non-sequitur. Buff Doge vs Cheems passed at risky tier.

**Rejected, with cause:** crude web-drawing family, four times, on art style. Anime stills, three times, twice from non-recognition. Single-image mood reactions, every instance. The Office, on source. 6-7, aura, mogging, Ohio, skibidi, rizz, all on presenter-register. Anakin and Padme, on identical panels. Armed-cartoon threat joke, on violence. Fake chat log with no visual punchline. Deadpan definition plates and live-data readouts, which were the 1.0 house style.

## Budget spent by deck

One row per deck, including decks that spent zero. A zero row is meaningful: it records that the budget was available and deliberately not used, which stops a later session from reading the absence as an oversight and over-correcting.

| Deck | Cohort | Slides | Budget | Used | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FSP Day 2, DWG 003 / 010 | FSP-2026 | 10 | 2 | 1 | Built before the standard existed. Second slot unspent |
| IDEA209H Unit 1.2 | IDEA209H-F26 | 12 logical, 36 physical | none, capped retired at 2.1 | 3, one cut | Slides 3, 6, 11. Gaps of two and four clean sheets. Three distinct structures: comparison, reveal, refusal |
| IDEA209H Unit 1.3, Day 7 | IDEA209H-F26 | 20 | none, ceilings retired at 2.1 | **0**, five generated and all five cut | Zero row, and a deliberate one. Three candidates reached Mr. Pina and all three were rejected, two more were cut by chat before proposal. Common cause across every one: no real local payload existed to build on. The Overheard log is empty and no class mistake, failed part, or shop phrase is on record anywhere chat can read, so the payload well was dry and chat generated plausible local color instead of saying so. This is the case behind `IDEA_HUMOR_STANDARDS.md` 2.2 |

## Changelog

- **1.4 (2026-08-25)** - Unit 1.3 (Day 7) recorded as a zero row. Five candidates, all
  cut, three of them by Mr. Pina on sight and two by chat before proposal. Every rejection
  is written with its cause, including the one where no cause was given, which is recorded
  as chat's hypothesis and explicitly labelled as not a rating. No cooldown is spent and
  the sourced-universe budget stays at one of two, stated in the cooldown block so a later
  session does not read five Unit 1.3 rows as five spent formats. The finding behind all
  of it went into `IDEA_HUMOR_STANDARDS.md` 2.2: with an empty Overheard log and no logged
  class material, the correct output of a humor pass is a zero row rather than invented
  local color.
- **1.3 (2026-08-25)** - **Void, never a real state.** Recorded the three Unit 1.3
  candidates as shipped and burned two cooldowns plus the cohort's entire sourced-universe
  budget on insertions that were rejected within the hour. Superseded by 1.4, which is
  rebuilt from 1.2 rather than edited forward, so the wrong cooldowns never have to be
  argued back out. If a 1.3 copy of this file exists anywhere, discard it.
- **1.2 (2026-08-25)** - First `IDEA209H-F26` entries, three shipped and one cut, written alongside `IDEA_HUMOR_STANDARDS.md` 2.1. Budget column now records that per-deck ceilings are retired while the cooldowns are not, since the two protect against different failures and only the ceiling was found to be measuring the wrong thing. Noted that a recurring in-house fixture authored by a colleague carries no reference cooldown, on the same footing as a house-cast character.
- **1.1 (2026-08-25)** - Two sections added alongside `IDEA_HUMOR_STANDARDS.md` 2.0. The Overheard log makes this file the currency authority, replacing web search, which produced a slate of six references that were all rejected as old or cringe. The Calibration record preserves the six rating rounds including the rejects with their causes, since chat re-proposed the crude-drawing family four times for want of a written reason. Reference cooldown now exempts house-cast characters, which is the operational reason the cast is worth building.
- **1.0 (2026-08-24)** - Initial ledger, created with `IDEA_HUMOR_STANDARDS.md` 1.0. Seeded with the FSP Day 2 Stark insertion, which is the only humor insertion known to have shipped in an IDEA artifact and is the case the standard was written from. Establishes the cohort list, the cross-cohort reuse rule, the derived live-cooldown block, and the per-deck budget table with its zero-row requirement.
